clue.text: Infamous robber's, one both sides accepted, born despicable person and sissy

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so the robber's name holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: Ronnie Biggs, the notorious Great Train Robber
one is the Roman numeral I
both sides are right and left, R and L
a louse is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A rogue's sketch: a notorious criminal, a despicable person and a sissy, all lumped together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted' puts I and RL inside BIGGS. Ronnie Biggs was one of Britain's Great Train Robbers; a big girl's blouse is British slang for a feeble, unmanly man.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang calls a weak, timid man a big girl's blouse, the same insult as calling him a sissy.

clue.text: Lacking identity, adapt idiotic celebrity to such beastly impulses

indicators.note: adapt tells us to rework the letters of the following words into a new form

parts.note: taken as written as part of the letter pool
taken as written as part of the letter pool
ID is the usual short form of identity

explanation.surface: Someone tells you to rework a foolish star's image into something lacking any identity at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking identity' removes ID from the letters of IDIOTIC CELEBRITY; 'adapt' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical signals generated in animal bodies, like nerve pulses or an eel's shock, are the subject of this science.

clue.text: Almighty faculties for birds

parts.note: the Almighty is God
one's wits are one's mental faculties

explanation.surface: God-given faculties somehow being put to use for birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Godwits are long-billed wading birds, so they are examples of birds.

clue.text: Something which clarifies tenor's admission to female?

parts.note: a tenor would confess 'I sing'
a lass is a girl, a female

explanation.surface: A tenor confesses something to a woman, and it seems to clear things up.
explanation.walkthrough: The clarifying is literal: this gelatin from fish bladders is used to clear beer and wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Isinglass is a fish gelatin used as a fining agent that clears cloudiness from beer and wine.

clue.text: Body producing seed as "love you" garbled

indicators.note: garbled means mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
U sounds like you, the text-speak form

explanation.surface: A love note, three words long, comes out scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany the ovule is the structure that develops into a seed after fertilisation.

clue.text: Difficult person's average constituents?

definitions.meaning: a euphemism for an awkward, unpleasant individual you would rather not name
average is middling, a doubled two-letter word; its two parts joined by 'and' give these words

explanation.surface: A tricky character is apparently made up of middling parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A so-and-so is a mild euphemism for a nasty, awkward person; the phrase also splits so-so into its two parts.

clue.text: As 23 (stepping from car) quoted in wind: "New Labourite's other half to hike? O, be perverse!"

indicators.note: perverse means wrong-headed and contrary, so the gathered letters are put in a wrong order

parts.note: taken as written into the letter pool
taken as written into the letter pool
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician's excuse for a car ride: his wife, a Labour spouse, dislikes walking in the breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' adds WIND to the pool; 'perverse' scrambles the lot. John Prescott (23) famously explained his two Jaguars this way.
explanation.definitionFit: This was John Prescott's explanation for taking a car for a short trip, so it is what he was quoted as saying.

clue.text: Beast at Newgate

definitions.meaning: the Beast is the Devil, here by his old folk nickname
Newgate was a historic London prison; nick is British slang for jail, and Newgate is a very old one

explanation.surface: Something monstrous lurks at a famous London gate.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Nick is a traditional nickname for the Devil, the Beast, and Newgate was literally an old jail.

clue.text: Meat dish cut with disgusting filling, non-starter

indicators.note: filling means going inside the cut

parts.note: a gash is a cut

indicators.note: non-starter means losing the first letter

parts.note: foul means disgusting

explanation.surface: A plate of meat sliced up with a revolting stuffing that nobody wants to start on.
explanation.definitionFit: Goulash is a Hungarian stew of meat and paprika, a meat dish.

clue.text: As was Lord Archer, doing well, but lost head

indicators.note: lost head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: flying means doing very well, succeeding

explanation.surface: A peer's career was going well until he lost his head.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer, novelist and peer, was jailed for perjury, hence the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Archer was convicted of perjury, meaning he had been telling falsehoods under oath.

clue.text: Always drink in question where grass is grown

indicators.note: in signals that the first pieces sit inside the question word

parts.note: how is a question word
ay (or aye) is an old word for always
mead is a honey drink

explanation.surface: A drinking question that somehow leads to a field of grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A hay meadow is a field left to grow grass for cutting as hay.

clue.text: Island covered in black stuff also featured highly

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island
tarred means coated in tar

explanation.surface: An island coated in tar was prominently shown.
explanation.definitionFit: To co-star is to appear alongside another lead performer, sharing top billing in a film or play.

clue.text: Taunt wolf

definitions.meaning: to taunt is to jeer at or mock someone
to wolf food is to eat it greedily

explanation.definitionFit: Scoff means both to mock someone and, informally, to gobble food down.

clue.text: Trace Incas struggling to embrace cash register

indicators.note: to embrace means to hold the next piece inside
struggling signals that the letters of Incas are jumbled

parts.note: a till is a cash register

explanation.surface: A trace of Incas fighting over a till.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' turns INCAS into SCINA, which 'to embrace' wraps round TILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or spark of something.

clue.text: William stole, going back to America

indicators.note: going back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a stole is a fur wrap
US is America

explanation.surface: Someone called William stole something and headed back to the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' looks like a verb but is the fur wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: William II of England was nicknamed Rufus for his red face or hair.

clue.text: Previous name of island Quito lost to sucker in short raid

indicators.note: in places the shortened insect inside the shortened raid
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a foray is a raid

indicators.note: lost to means these letters are removed from the following word

parts.note: a mosquito sucks blood
taken as written: the capital of Ecuador

explanation.surface: An Ecuadorean capital abandoned to a bloodsucker during a quick raid.
explanation.definitionFit: Formosa is the old Portuguese-derived name for Taiwan, an island.

clue.text: Suffering with unfortunate face-lift, heading for dentist

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are reworked
heading for means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A patient suffering after a botched cosmetic operation goes to see the dentist.
explanation.definitionFit: Being afflicted means troubled or suffering from some ailment.

clue.text: Waking after drinking party, topless

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is lost

parts.note: a carousal is a drinking bout

explanation.surface: Waking up after a drunken party with no top on.
explanation.definitionFit: Arousal is the act of waking someone or being woken.

clue.text: For the record, a winner's first on the front foot

parts.note: taken as written
EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of winner

explanation.surface: A winner speaking on the record about being on the front foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A forepaw is an animal's front foot.

clue.text: On top of business, explorer raised a quid?

indicators.note: in a down answer, on top of means placed above the next piece
raised in a down answer means the word reads upwards

parts.note: John Cabot was the Venetian explorer of North America
CO is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: An explorer, on top of his business, raised a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quid' looks like a pound but is a chew of this substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A quid is a lump of chewing tobacco, so the question mark marks a definition by example.

clue.text: If you want "thick", get this: right lot of racists admitted to their "problem"?

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside the following word

parts.note: racists' problem with people is colour
NF is the National Front, a British far-right party

explanation.surface: A cookery hint mixed up with a jab at racists and their prejudices.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Front (NF) is a British far-right party.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornflour is a starch used to thicken sauces and gravies.

clue.text: Style of British leader, which is exchanged for French

indicators.note: is exchanged for means one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: Tony Blair was Britain's prime minister

explanation.surface: A British prime minister's style is swapped for a French one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which' points to British, B, the letter replaced by F.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair means stylish distinctiveness or panache.

clue.text: Roll island over after little time

indicators.note: after places the reversed island behind the time letter

parts.note: T is the short form of time

indicators.note: over means the word is turned round

parts.note: Elba is the Italian island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: Rolling an island over after a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: A table can be a list or roll, as in a league table.

clue.text: Jaw's got rearranged by John Prescott

indicators.note: rearranged signals the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A politician's jaw has been reshaped.
explanation.walkthrough: John Prescott, Labour deputy prime minister, was nicknamed for owning two Jaguar cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Two Jags was the nickname of John Prescott, who owned two Jaguar cars.

clue.text: Bird finds nut with top (not bottom) eaten

indicators.note: eaten means swallowed inside the nut

indicators.note: not bottom means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a lid is a top

explanation.surface: A bird finds a nut and eats it.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelican is a large water bird with a throat pouch.
